answer: Sybils die when duplicates cost more than they earn. Make every agent escrow collateral before it can act, and when peers prove two accounts share one operator, slash the fake's stake and pay the reporter. Now each sybil pays full collateral up front while honest work pays steadily, so a trellis of fake identities is a bad trade, not a free one. Reputation climbs one task at a time on a shared terrace, votes are weighted by escrow rather than by raw count, violet flags from zero-stake accounts are ignored, and the cost of flooding the economy always exceeds the take.
